digest.en: Lula defeats Bolsonaro in Brazil, securing a fourth term as the former president refuses to concede. In Kyiv, Russian strikes hit a dormitory, killing one person and underscoring the persistent threat to civilian infrastructure.
digest.hi: चक्रवात अर्नब ने आज उत्तराखंड, हिमाचल प्रदेश और पंजाब के तटवर्ती क्षेत्रों में तेज़ हवाओं और भारी बारिश लाकर आपातकालीन चेतावनी जारी की।

articles.title: Ukraine Says One Dead As Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv Civilian Buildings Including Dormitory
articles.summary: Russian air strikes hit Kyiv on October 26, targeting a university dormitory and other civilian buildings. At least one person died in the attacks. President Zelenskyy urged international partners to supply Ukraine with adequate defensive capabilities. Russian air attacks struck Kyiv late on October 26, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites, leaving at least one dead, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Ukraine's partners to provide the "proper tools" for the country to defend itself.

articles.title: India's IT firms face a new dilemma: How to train tomorrow's engineers in the age of AI
articles.summary: Major Indian IT companies are reducing fresh graduate hiring as artificial intelligence alters required skill sets. Industry leaders warn this trend risks a future shortage of experienced engineers. Universities and firms must collaborate to develop new talent pipelines. India’s biggest IT firms are hiring far fewer fresh graduates, as AI changes the skills employers seek. Industry experts tell CNA this could create a shortage of experienced workers in the future unless companies and universities do more to develop young talent.

articles.title: Netanyahu, wanted by ICC, battles for political survival as Israel goes to the polls
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces elections while wanted by the International Criminal Court. Public dissatisfaction over the Hamas attack and high living costs has weakened his support. The vote will determine his political future and Likud's standing. Public anger over failure to prevent the Hamas attack, an inconclusive war, and the rising costs of living have eroded Netanyahu’s standing at home and abroad; the outcome of this poll is likely to shape the longest-serving PM’s political future, the fate of Likud and the legal challenges he faces.

articles.title: World leaders congratulate Lula on historic election win as Bolsonaro refuses to concede
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro rejected the Brazilian election results, calling it impossible to concede the loss. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth non-consecutive term. The far-right senator lost the second round to the leftist president. The electoral court confirmed the final tally. Leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated the far-right senator and was elected president of Brazil for a fourth non-consecutive termFull report: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil’s president over Flávio BolsonaroLive second round resultsThe local electoral court ordered the immediate restoration of 100% of the bus fleet and ordered the arrest of the municipal transport secretary, Pablo S.

articles.title: Lula defeats far-right Bolsonaro to secure a fourth presidential term
articles.summary: Lula defeated Bolsonaro to win a fourth term as Brazil's president. The result secures his return to power after a contentious campaign. This victory shifts the country's political direction back toward the center-left. Lula wins a historic fourth term in Brazil, Serbia’s ruling party is ousted after student-led protests, and Marine Le Pen launches her presidential bid in France. Meanwhile, Israel votes in parliamentary elections amid uncertainty over Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition.

articles.title: What Now For Serbia After Vucic's Stunning Election Defeat?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic lost the Serbian parliamentary elections to student-led opposition. The ruling party was ousted from power. The new government must now navigate complex relations with the European Union, Russia, and China. Who will lead the next government of Serbia, after Aleksandar Vucic lost parliamentary elections, can the protest movement turn electoral success into stable rule, and what the result could mean for Serbia’s balancing relations with the European Union, Russia, and China?

articles.title: UN-commissioned experts say Gaza ceasefire has not stopped Israel from committing genocide
articles.summary: UN experts concluded the Gaza ceasefire did not stop Israeli actions constituting genocide. The Commission of Inquiry issued these findings. Prosecutors at the International Criminal Court may use the report to pursue legal action against officials. The findings by the Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory could be used by prosecutors at the International Criminal Court or in other jurisdictions to try to bring justice to victims and their relatives.

articles.title: Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting
articles.summary: Mecca Defense Alliance partners met in Tehran to address regional conflicts. The snap meeting focused on stabilizing the Middle East. These tensions are currently disrupting global oil and cargo flows across the region. Officials from the so-called Mecca Defense Alliance have gathered for a snap meeting in Tehran as they look to settle conflicts in the Middle East that have left the region reeling and are impacting global flows of oil and other cargo.

articles.title: U.K. PM Burnham backs principle of ‘earned settlement’ in immigration rules
articles.summary: U. K. PM Burnham supported the earned settlement principle for immigration. The proposal increases the baseline qualifying period for permanent residency. This change was part of a draft overhaul introduced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. An increase in the baseline qualifying period for settlement, from 5 of 15 years had been proposed by U. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood as part of a draft “earned settlement” immigration overhaul last year, during the Keir Starmer administration.

articles.title: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
articles.summary: A panel of human rights experts concluded that Russian forces committed war crimes and crimes against humanity during the Ukraine invasion. The findings cite deliberate attacks on civilians and vital energy infrastructure. These actions violate international law. The report details specific violations of protected targets. Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

articles.title: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
articles.summary: The United Nations reported that women and girls accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year. This figure represents a doubling of their share compared to 2021. The data highlights a significant shift in the demographic impact of global wars. Civilian casualties have risen sharply during this period. War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.

articles.title: US forces accused of ‘weaponising’ Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children in the path of
articles.summary: US airstrikes in southern Somalia are pushing civilians toward the rising River Juba. Women and children face drowning risks as they flee al-Shabaab territory. Humanitarian groups accuse the military of weaponizing the flood crisis. The strategy traps vulnerable populations in dangerous waterways. Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety.

articles.title: Bizarre hobby takes seed among China’s stressed young adults
articles.summary: Chinese young adults are increasingly adopting bricks as a low-cost hobby to replace pets or children. This trend stems from a stagnant job market and financial pressure. The practice offers a cheap, low-maintenance outlet for stress. It serves as a symbolic alternative to traditional responsibilities. Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’Young adults in China looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having children or pets have found an answer: raising bricks. Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing.

articles.title: Why Lula’s ‘miracle’ win matters well beyond Brazil
articles.summary: Lula secured a surprising victory over Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil. The win reversed a significant first-round deficit. It signals a major shift in global politics. The outcome impacts climate policy and international relations beyond South America. Three weeks ago, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s political obituaries had all been written. The far-right presidential candidate, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, had come out of the first round of the presidential election with a lead that looked impossible to overcome.

articles.title: Does Japan need nuclear subs? The debate is bigger than China
articles.summary: Japan is debating the acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi opened the discussion in parliament. The decision is part of a 2026 security review. The debate extends beyond countering China to broader strategic autonomy. Japan’s debate over nuclear-powered submarines is gaining momentum, but political deliberation should not be mistaken for a done deal. As Tokyo prepares to revise its three principal national security documents by the end of 2026, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has opened the door to a long-politically sensitive capability.

articles.title: Student-Led Opposition Celebrates In Serbia After Vucic Concedes Election Defeat
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections. The student-led Students' List took a decisive lead in preliminary results. This ends his fourteen-year dominance of Serbian politics. Former President Aleksandar Vucic, who dominated Serbian politics for the past 14 years, conceded defeat in the country's parliamentary elections after polls closed on October 25. Preliminary results showed the movement called Students' List taking a decisive lead.

articles.title: Vucic Concedes Electoral Defeat, Setting Stage For New Era Of Serbian Politics, Relations With West
articles.summary: Vucic admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in Serbia's parliamentary vote. His concession signals a potential shift toward European alignment. The new government may distance Serbia from Kremlin influence. Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's former president and dominant political figure for more than a decade, conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in the country's parliamentary elections, potentially ushering in a new era of politics more closely aligned with Europe and away from the Kremlin.

articles.title: Relentless Russian Strikes Drive Civilians From Ukraine's Kramatorsk
articles.summary: Ukraine ordered mandatory evacuations for families with children in Kramatorsk and Slovyansk. Russian forces intensified strikes across the Donetsk region. The move aims to protect civilians as Moscow pushes to seize the entire area. As Russian forces intensify attacks on Ukraine’s Donetsk region, evacuations are accelerating in Kramatorsk, a key city still held by Kyiv. As Moscow seeks to seize all of the Donetsk region, Ukraine has issued a mandatory evacuation order for families with children in Kramatorsk and Slovyansk.

articles.title: After Starshield Disruptions, Zelenskyy Says Satellite Communications Now Fully Functional
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed on October 24 that Starshield and Starlink systems are fully operational. The satellite communications, developed by SpaceX, had been disrupted for over a week. This outage limited Ukraine's defensive operations during the period. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on October 24 that the Starshield and Starlink satellite systems were back to normal operations. Disruptions in the communications systems, developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company, had limited Ukraine's defensive operations for over a week.

articles.title: Bipartisan US Lawmakers Push Back On Trump's Russia Policy, Vow Support For Ukraine
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers challenged President Trump's easing of Russian energy import restrictions. They demanded guarantees that Ukraine retains access to critical American military and intelligence support. The move signals growing congressional resistance to the administration's shifting foreign policy stance on the conflict. A bipartisan group of US lawmakers is stepping up efforts to defend Ukraine, challenging President Donald Trump’s decision to ease restrictions on Russian energy imports and demanding guarantees that Kyiv will retain access to critical American military and intelligence support.

articles.title: Kim Jong-un crosses newly opened bridge into China
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un crossed the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge into China. He arrived in the border city of Dandong to meet senior Communist party officials. The visit marked the inauguration of the new crossing and signaled a push to expand bilateral cooperation between the two nations. North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party memberKim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour. The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification.

articles.title: Women ‘first to suffer’ under siege, first to step up as frontline responders in Sudan
articles.summary: Tahani Al-Numeiri in Khartoum mistook the initial explosions for wedding celebrations on 15 April 2023. The Rapid Support Forces had just opened fire on the army. Women in Sudan now serve as frontline responders during the siege. They face immediate danger while managing critical aid distribution. The conflict has forced them into roles previously held by men. Their work sustains communities under active bombardment.

articles.title: Green batteries built on dirty dealings in Indonesia
articles.summary: Leaked documents reveal Harita Group paid for goodwill on Obi island to secure nickel for electric vehicle batteries. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project published the files on October 22. These payments facilitated mining operations that supply a growing share of global battery production. A growing share of the world’s electric-vehicle batteries contains nickel from Obi, an Indonesian island where the mining company Harita Group has long paid for goodwill, according to alleged leaked documents published on October 22 by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP).

articles.title: China bets refitted destroyers can hold line in US numbers race
articles.summary: China is refitting older destroyers to maintain fleet mass against the United States. The People's Liberation Army Navy completed extensive midlife upgrades on surface combatants this month. This approach prioritizes preserving numbers over purely qualitative technological modernization in naval warfare. Recent midlife upgrades to China’s older surface combatants highlight an ongoing debate over whether preserving naval fleet mass provides an operational edge over purely qualitative technological modernization in naval warfare.

articles.title: Why ultra‑Orthodox parties will decide Netanyahu’s electoral fate
articles.summary: Israeli authorities detained dozens of Haredi men on 20 October 2026, a week before national elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the draft evasion arrests as unacceptable. The incident highlights the political leverage ultra-Orthodox parties hold over Netanyahu's electoral prospects following a 2024 court ruling on military service exemptions. On October 20, 2026, a week before Israel’s elections, dozens of men were detained on suspicion of evading the draft – arrests that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called “unacceptable.” The young men attend ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, religious schools, whose students were long exempt from the military service mandatory for most Israelis.
